data.title: When Jorge Luis Borges met one of the founders of AI
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕博尔赫斯的作品及其与人工智能（LLM）关系的讨论

不同观点：
• [viccis] 推荐博尔赫斯的作品，尤其是《特隆、乌克巴尔、奥尔比斯·特蒂乌斯》和《迷宫》，并提到目前英语最佳版本是《企鹅现代作家全集》。他还讨论了博尔赫斯与LLM（大型语言模型）的关系，认为即使拥有博尔赫斯的全部阅读和感官数据，也无法创造出博尔赫斯式的先验知识，因为这涉及到康德的认识论问题。

• [karaterobot] 对LLM能否通过深入理解博尔赫斯的生活来重现其作品表示好奇，并认为这是一个有趣的创意故事，或许未来LLM可以实现这一点。

• [101008] 推荐博尔赫斯，但认为其英文翻译缺乏原作的诗意和音乐性，庆幸自己的母语是西班牙语。

• [kouru225] 推荐博尔赫斯的短篇小说《博闻强记的富内斯》，并分享了链接。

• [jhbadger] 对网站使用的图片实际上是克劳德·香农表示困惑，并提供了相关链接。

• [tekacs] 推荐了一篇关于博尔赫斯与人工智能的论文，并提供了链接。

• [jl6] 提到霍夫斯塔特应该写一本关于博尔赫斯的书，并分享了自己关于博尔赫斯与AI等主题的写作链接。

• [david_shi] 引用了博尔赫斯的《阿莱夫》中的一段文字，展示了博尔赫斯作品中的深邃意象。

• [netsharc] 认为博尔赫斯的故事有时像是在报告某种假设情境，如果这篇讨论是对博尔赫斯的致敬，那将非常有趣。

• [6stringmerc] 提到在狱中阅读萨特的《存在与虚无》，认为LLM若经过萨特作品的训练，可能会产生令人不安的逻辑推论，反映人类思想和行为的不完美状态。

• [integralof5y] 认为博尔赫斯和赫伯特·西蒙都是伟大的思想家，但他们关于人类与机器智能的对话并不深入，LLM为我们提供了探索智能与语言关系的新工具。

补充讨论：
• [mentalgear] 询问是否有该访谈的音频文件，表示更喜欢听原版内容。

争议焦点：
• 博尔赫斯作品能否通过LLM重现：[viccis]和[karaterobot]对此持不同意见，前者认为即使拥有数据也无法重现博尔赫斯的先验知识，而后者则认为这是一个有趣的潜在发展。

• 翻译问题：[101008] 认为博尔赫斯的英文翻译缺乏原作的诗意和音乐性，这引发了对翻译质量的讨论。

• 博尔赫斯与人工智能的关系：[tekacs]和[jl6]提供了相关论文和链接，扩展了博尔赫斯作品与现代AI技术的联系。

• 访谈图片错误：[jhbadger] 指出了网站图片的错误，并提供了相关链接，这涉及到对历史人物的正确识别问题。

这些讨论展示了博尔赫斯作品的多重维度和其在现代技术背景下的新意义。

data.title: Search could be so much better. And I don't mean chatbots with web access
data.author: mfkhalil
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种新型搜索引擎MatterRank，其核心特点是让用户能够控制搜索结果的排序，而不仅仅是让算法猜测用户的需求。传统的搜索引擎通过关键词、链接和各种信号来猜测用户意图，而MatterRank允许用户用自己的语言描述如何排序结果，提供更个性化和精准的搜索体验。这不是一个简单的聊天机器人或智能自动补全工具，而是一种全新的搜索方式，让用户决定什么最重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：搜索引擎的使用体验和功能改进

不同观点：
• [q0uaur] 认为该搜索引擎的概念不错，但怀疑其每次查询的成本较高。测试时要求排除大科技公司和广告，但结果中仍出现YouTube和Reddit，质疑算法是否真正过滤了域名。
• [maximumgeek] 批评该帖缺乏上下文，认为搜索结果仍需改进，尤其是广告和无用结果的过滤问题。对Quora答案和此类宣传帖感到厌烦。
• [SteveDavis88] 希望有一个能严格按照指定关键词返回结果的搜索引擎，认为谷歌无法满足这一点。
• [renegat0x0] 讨论了使用大型SQLite数据库进行域名搜索的可能性，但承认面临垃圾信息和过滤的挑战，类似于谷歌的处理方式。
• [danpalmer] 不同意搜索引擎假设用户不知道自己想要什么的说法，认为这是对搜索引擎体验的误解。
• [mfkhalil] 支持使用MatterRank，认为其能提供超越关键词匹配的定性特征结果，例如特定内容过滤，提供更高的搜索精度。
• [AymanJabr] 批评需要注册和创建引擎的步骤，希望直接使用搜索功能，不关心保存引擎供日后使用。
• [karmakaze] 质疑该帖是否为宣传广告，认为缺乏技术内容，未解释为何MatterRank优于Perplexity。
• [janalsncm] 认为使用LLM（大型语言模型）进行排名虽然结果质量较高，但速度较慢，建议通过过滤低质量内容和使用神经网络提高速度。
• [BrenBarn] 认为不仅是搜索引擎，现代技术普遍存在告诉用户该做什么的趋势，而非让用户自主决定。
• [eternauta3k] 质疑在每个结果上运行LLM的成本是否过高。
• [vivzkestrel] 提出Kagi与MatterRank的比较问题。
• [skeptrune] 询问是否存在某种交叉编码器用于评分提示。
• [TekMol] 坚决反对需要创建账户才能使用搜索引擎的做法。

补充讨论：
• 搜索结果的质量和相关性是主要关注点，尤其是广告和低质量内容的过滤。
• 用户普遍对需要注册或创建账户的搜索引擎持负面态度。
• 不同用户对LLM的使用持不同看法，有人认为能提高结果质量，有人认为速度太慢。
• 对MatterRank的功能和优势存在争议，部分用户质疑其宣传效果。
• 比较不同搜索引擎（如Kagi和MatterRank）的讨论显示用户对搜索引擎的选择和偏好存在差异。

43563915.article_content:
Search could be so much better
And I don't mean chatbots with access to a search engine.
Search is suffering from a quiet, unfortunate assumption. One that made the internet accessible to billions—but made it much less personal than it could be.
It assumes we don't know what we want.
This isn't search engines' fault. For decades, the only way we could communicate what we wanted was through a little search box.
So they did their best. They built systems to guess what we meant—ranking pages based on overlapping words, backlinks, reputation, and a hundred other signals. The best version of that became PageRank. And it was so good, it powered one of the most valuable companies in history.
But then computers learned how to understand language.
Now, we can do something new: we can tell search engines not just what we want, but
how we want it ranked
.
MatterRank is the first search engine where you control the ranking—using your own words.
This isn't a chatbot that summarizes results. And it's not just smarter autocomplete.
It's a new kind of search engine—one that lets you decide what matters most.
Let me know what you uncover. My email's below.
—Moe Khalil
Founder of MatterRank
moe@matterrank.ai
Try it now!
...or read more about how it works
→

data.title: Aptera's First Solar Road Trip. 300 Miles, One Charge
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Aptera成功完成了其首次太阳能支持的公路旅行，单次充电行驶超过300英里，展示了太阳能电动车不仅是未来概念，更是当前可行的解决方案。这趟旅程从亚利桑那州的弗拉格斯塔夫出发，经过历史悠久的66号公路，途经金曼和哈瓦苏湖，最终返回加州。尽管有些时候是多云天气，车辆仍能产生超过545瓦的太阳能输入。车辆在各种路况下表现优异，包括山路、高速公路和乡村道路。此次旅行不仅验证了Aptera系统在现实条件下的可靠性，还展示了重新思考交通工具的潜力。为了庆祝这次成功，Aptera还举办了一项抽奖活动，奖品包括价值800美元的太阳能套装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动汽车（EV）上安装太阳能板的实用性及可行性，特别是Aptera车型的设计和生产问题。

不同观点：
• 支持太阳能板在EV上的应用：
  - [torginus] 认为在EV上安装太阳能板非常实用，即使只能产生几百瓦的电力，也能满足日常通勤需求，减少插电次数。
  - [ZeroGravitas] 指出太阳能板在某些特定领域（如冷藏车、高尔夫球车）已经得到应用，并且未来有增长潜力。

• 对Aptera车型及生产问题的关注：
  - [arrakark] 赞赏Aptera的愿景，但对车型的量产能力和资金问题表示担忧。
  - [underseacables] 表示对Aptera的喜爱，但认为像BYD和Tesla这样的公司会占据大部分市场份额，且Aptera在融资方面遇到了困难。

• 对太阳能板效率和设计的质疑：
  - [pinkmuffinere] 通过计算质疑太阳能板在实际使用中的效率，认为即使在理想条件下，所产生的电量也不足以支持长距离行驶。
  - [dontlaugh] 对Aptera车身尺寸和设计提出质疑，认为其过大。
  - [dscottboggs] 强烈反对在EV上安装太阳能板，认为这不仅增加成本，且无法支持车辆在实际道路条件下的行驶需求。

• 其他创新设计建议：
  - [xnx] 提出了一种替代方案，即使用拖挂式太阳能板，以增加太阳能发电量并适用于任何EV。

• 历史案例的提及：
  - [jore] 提到了德国初创公司Sono Motors的类似项目，虽然该公司已经破产，但其太阳能板项目仍在继续。

• 对市场接受度的讨论：
  - [mlsu] 认为Aptera这样的高效能汽车虽然设计优美，但市场接受度可能不高，因为大多数消费者更关注价格和实用性。

• 对特朗普和马斯克曾提出的太阳能车顶概念的讨论：
  - [trhway] 分析了Trump和Musk曾提出的太阳能车顶概念，认为如果成本接近零，这种设计对日常通勤是有意义的，但目前实现起来成本过高。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到Aptera的生产和资金问题，反映出对该车型能否成功量产的普遍担忧。
- 对太阳能板在实际应用中的效率问题进行了详细计算和分析，显示出对其实用性的质疑。
- 有人提出创新的设计方案，如拖挂式太阳能板，以解决现有设计中的效率问题。

43533556.article_content:
300+ Miles, One Charge, Supported by the Sun’s Rays
Aptera just completed its first-ever solar-supported road trip—driving over 300 miles on a single charge and proving that a solar EV isn’t just a concept for the future, but a real-world solution ready for the present.
Our Co-CEO Steve Fambro, along with a small crew, took Aptera’s production-intent vehicle on a road trip through the American Southwest. They started early in the snowy mountain town of Flagstaff, Arizona, where the vehicle was already pulling in 300 watts of solar energy before the day even began.
The route followed a stretch of historic Route 66—quiet roads, breathtaking scenery, and a test bed for a vehicle built to thrive independently. “It’s kind of the path not really taken,” Steve shared. “And that’s one of the reasons we wanted to do it this way.”
From Flagstaff to Hackberry, through Kingman and down to sunny Lake Havasu, Aptera performed with quiet confidence. Even on an overcast day, the team saw over 545 watts of solar input. That means more time exploring and less time searching for chargers.
During its 300+ mile journey, the vehicle handled every condition thrown at it: mountain passes, 18-wheelers, potholes, desert winds, highways, and winding country roads.
“The panoramic windshield gives you this incredible view of the landscape,” Steve said, describing the drive. “It’s like a big picture window into the future.”
The final stretch took the team back into California, where they reflected on the journey, the data, and the excited reactions from drivers who caught a glimpse of the vehicle on the road. “Almost everyone we passed had their phones out filming us,” Steve laughed. “It’s clear that Aptera’s design stops traffic—without needing to stop for a charge.”
This trip marks a huge milestone for Aptera, not only in validating our systems in real-world conditions but in showing what’s possible when you rethink transportation from the ground up. With every mile driven by our production-intent vehicles, we’re one step closer to a future where every journey is powered by the sun.

主要讨论点：北朝鲜黑客利用加密货币进行盗窃行为及其引发的相关讨论

不同观点：
• 一方认为黑客的行为是合理利用加密货币的规则，不应视为作弊。例如，horacemorace和chasing指出，黑客的行为是在遵循加密货币“自我监管”的规则，称其为“作弊”是一种输不起的心态。ForHackernews进一步认为，区块链作为透明且不可篡改的账本，不能将这些交易视为“ cheating”、“crime”或“theft”。

• 另一方则关注加密货币系统的脆弱性和安全性问题。abidhusain强调，国家背景的黑客对加密货币世界的攻击日益频繁，显示出该系统仍然非常脆弱。IncreasePosts则指出，北韩的经济很大程度上依赖于加密货币盗窃，这一现象令人担忧。

• 还有观点聚焦于对加密货币的整体批评和不信任。josefritzishere认为，加密货币缺乏如传统银行系统的FDIC保障，被盗资金难以追回，显示出其作为货币的缺陷。

补充讨论：
• 部分讨论提到了对北韩黑客技术水平的评价。starwin1159质疑北韩黑客的技术是否属于顶级，而bjornsing则以历史事件为例，指出北韩此前也有过不诚信行为。

• 对于制裁与犯罪基础设施的讨论，rchaud提到美国解除对Tornado Cash制裁的时机，指出犯罪依赖于特定基础设施，而简单地“锁起来”并不是解决方案。

• 最后，有些评论提供了额外的资源和建议。benrutter推荐了BBC的Lazarus Heist播客以了解北韩黑客行为，而OutOfHere则对WazirX冷钱包的安全性提出质疑。

争议焦点：黑客行为是否构成作弊，以及加密货币系统应如何应对安全挑战。

data.title: Curl-impersonate: Special build of curl that can impersonate the major browsers
data.author: mmh0000
data.article_summary:
`curl-impersonate` 是一个修改版的 curl，能够模拟 Chrome、Firefox、Edge 和 Safari 四大浏览器。它通过调整 TLS 和 HTTP 握手过程，使其与真实浏览器的表现完全一致，从而绕过网站对客户端进行的 TLS 和 HTTP/2 指纹识别。该工具可以像常规 curl 一样从命令行使用，也可以作为库集成到项目中替代常规的 libcurl。

为了实现模拟，`curl-impersonate` 做了以下修改：
1. 使用与浏览器相同的 TLS 库（如 Firefox 的 NSS 和 Chrome 的 BoringSSL）。
2. 调整 TLS 扩展和 SSL 选项。
3. 修改 HTTP/2 连接设置。
4. 使用特定标志运行，如 `--ciphers` 和 `--curves`。

该工具支持多个版本的浏览器，并提供了包装脚本方便使用。详细使用方法和支持的浏览器列表可以在文档中找到。

• 指纹识别技术在不同网络层的可行性和防御措施的有效性。

总体来看，讨论围绕curl-impersonate的改进、应用、潜在风险和防御措施展开，涉及技术细节和实际应用场景。

curl-impersonate
A special build of
curl
that can impersonate the four major browsers: Chrome, Edge, Safari & Firefox. curl-impersonate is able to perform TLS and HTTP handshakes that are identical to that of a real browser.
curl-impersonate can be used either as a command line tool, similar to the regular curl, or as a library that can be integrated instead of the regular libcurl. See
Usage
below.
Why?
When you use an HTTP client with a TLS website, it first performs a TLS handshake. The first message of that handshake is called Client Hello. The Client Hello message that most HTTP clients and libraries produce differs drastically from that of a real browser.
If the server uses HTTP/2, then in addition to the TLS handshake there is also an HTTP/2 handshake where various settings are exchanged. The settings that most HTTP clients and libraries use differ as well from those of any real browsers.
For these reasons, some web services use the TLS and HTTP handshakes to fingerprint which client is accessing them, and then present different content for different clients. These methods are known as
TLS fingerprinting
and
HTTP/2 fingerprinting
respectively. Their widespread use has led to the web becoming less open, less private and much more restrictive towards specific web clients
With the modified curl in this repository, the TLS and HTTP handshakes look
exactly
like those of a real browser.
How?
To make this work,
curl
was patched significantly to resemble a browser. Specifically, The modifications that were needed to make this work:
Compiling curl with nss, the TLS library that Firefox uses, instead of OpenSSL. For the Chrome version, compiling with BoringSSL, Google's TLS library.
Modifying the way curl configures various TLS extensions and SSL options.
Adding support for new TLS extensions.
Changing the settings that curl uses for its HTTP/2 connections.
Running curl with some non-default flags, for example
--ciphers
,
--curves
and some
-H
headers.
The resulting curl looks, from a network perspective, identical to a real browser.
Read the full technical description in the blog posts:
part a
,
part b
.

For each supported browser there is a wrapper script that launches

Please note that the wrapper scripts use a default set of HTTP headers. If you want to change these headers, you may want to modify the wrapper scripts to fit your own purpose.

data.title: Show HN: The C3 programming language (C alternative language)
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: C3是一种基于C语言语法和语义的编程语言，旨在进化C语言的同时保持C程序员熟悉的特性。C3强调与C语言的ABI兼容性，可以轻松在同一项目中混合使用C和C3代码。其设计原则包括保持C语言的核心特性，仅在必要时进行修改，并引入一些高层次的便利功能。C3没有强制性的头文件，采用基于模块的命名空间，支持切片、编译时反射、增强的编译时执行、基于泛型模块的泛型编程、基于"Result"类型的零开销错误处理、延迟执行（defer）、值方法、关联枚举数据等特性。C3的灵感来源于C2语言，旨在迭代C语言而不是创造一种全新的语言。预编译的二进制文件适用于Windows x64、Debian x64、Ubuntu x86和MacOS Arm64等操作系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对C3编程语言的评价与讨论，包括语法、功能、与类似语言的对比以及对特定语言特性的需求和建议。

不同观点：
• [sfpotter] 认为使用 `::` 语法很丑陋，支持像D语言那样统一使用 `.`。他强调了简洁语法的重要性。
• [micklemeal] 实际使用后觉得C3在整合C库方面表现最好，尤其是与raylib和libtmx的整合，并对C3未来获得更多认可抱有期待。
• [dooglius] 提出C3与Zig、Odin的对比，这些语言都有改进C的相同目标，并质疑C3能否获得同样的关注。
• [Sohcahtoa82] 喜欢C3在switch/case行为上的改变，但对使用 `fn` 定义函数的必要性提出疑问，并表示如果需要用C语言时会考虑C3。

补充讨论：
• [dkersten] 对C3的整体印象积极，但对某些语法选择（如函数定义格式）有不同偏好，理解其设计背后的原因。
• [johnisgood] 关心标准库的贡献（如添加BLAKE2）以及如何使用不同的哈希算法实现“rehash”，并对线程安全的哈希表是否能进入标准库表示关注。
• [moktonar] 对使用 `fn` 标记函数定义的必要性提出疑问。
• [unclad5968] 使用C3后觉得不错，但希望有标记联合类型，并提到该特性已在计划中。
• [CyberDildonics] 认为系统语言应具备泛型、析构函数和所有权三个特性，而C3只具备泛型，对此表示遗憾。
• [accelbred] 关心是否能实现弱函数以及是否支持类似GCC的构造函数属性。
• [owlstuffing] 认为C3在处理宏和条件编译方面不够理想，质疑其设计选择。
• [djmips] 询问是否支持原生的定点类型。
• [alcover] 询问如何表达只读指针，类似于C语言中的 `const int* ptr`。
• [xormapmap] 认为许多C替代语言添加了过多复杂特性，主张C的改进版应保持简单，去除不必要的复杂性并改进C的设计缺陷。

争议焦点：
• 语法选择，尤其是 `::` 和 `fn` 的使用，部分开发者认为这些增加了不必要的复杂性。
• 与Zig、Odin等类似语言的对比，讨论C3能否脱颖而出。
• 对C3应具备哪些核心系统语言特性的不同看法，如是否需要所有权和析构函数。

这些讨论反映了开发者对C3的不同期望和需求，尤其是关于语言设计和功能实现的争议。

C3 Language
C3 is a programming language that builds on the syntax and semantics of the C language,
with the goal of evolving it while still retaining familiarity for C programmers.
It's an evolution, not a revolution: the C-like
for programmers who like C.
Precompiled binaries for the following operating systems are available:
Windows x64
download

Debian x64
download

Ubuntu x86
download

install instructions
.
MacOS Arm64
download
,
install instructions
.
The manual for C3 can be found at
www.c3-lang.org
.
Thanks to full ABI compatibility with C, it's possible to mix C and C3 in the same project with no effort. As a demonstration, vkQuake was compiled with a small portion of the code converted to C3 and compiled with the c3c compiler. (The fork can be found at
https://github.com/c3lang/vkQuake
)
Design Principles
Procedural "get things done"-type of language.
Try to stay close to C - only change what's really necessary.
C ABI compatibility and excellent C integration.
Learning C3 should be easy for a C programmer.
Data is inert.
Avoid "big ideas" & the "more is better" fallacy.
Introduce some higher level conveniences where the value is great.
C3 owes its inspiration to the
C2 language
: to iterate on top of C without trying to be a
whole new language.

The following code shows
generic modules
(more examples can be found at
https://c3-lang.org/references/docs/examples/
).

Stack
{
usz capacity;

Define our new types, the first will implicitly create

No mandatory header files
New semantic macro system
Module based name spacing
Slices
Compile time reflection
Enhanced compile time execution
Generics based on generic modules
"Result"-based zero overhead error handling

Value methods

主要讨论点：用户对一款具有赛博朋克风格的语音/文本聊天应用的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [b0bben] 认为当前的程序无聊，想打造一个具有赛博朋克风格的社区平台。他描述了自己正在开发的项目，尽管还在早期阶段，但他对开发过程感到非常兴奋，并希望吸引更多人从Discord转移到他的平台。他也表达了希望将该项目发展成一个真正的产品并以此为生的愿望。

• [panja] 对隐私问题表示关注，特别是用户数据的管理方式，询问是否有端到端加密（e2ee）的计划。

• [Layogtima] 对项目表示喜爱，询问是否会开源，并表示有兴趣将其用于模拟Vogon Constructor Fleet船舰的界面。

• [jagermo] 建议添加骰子滚动功能和别名功能，以便于进行Shadowrun或Cyberpunk等桌面角色扮演游戏。

• [egypturnash] 对视频示例中缺少实际图片表示失望，但个人风格上认可该项目的赛博朋克风格。

• [jamauro] 和 [indigoabstract] 都对项目表示赞赏和鼓励，认为其风格酷似黑客游戏的用户界面。

• [cyberpunk] 以幽默的方式表达了对项目风格的认可，但也指出项目缺少一些与他个人品牌相关的标志性元素，如九寸钉乐队T恤、破洞牛仔裤、对字体和耳机的独特品味等。

data.title: AI cheats: Why you didn't notice your teammate was cheating
data.author: duckling23
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了游戏作弊技术的发展，特别是从内存读取的 aimbots 到基于颜色的 colorbots，再到如今的AI辅助瞄准。作者 vike256 分享了自己在游戏作弊领域的经验，包括早期使用 Android 手机制作作弊程序，以及后来开发了开源 colorbot "Unibot"。Colorbots 通过分析屏幕上的颜色来识别敌人，但并不适用于所有游戏。AI 作弊则是 colorbots 的进化版，利用训练过的AI模型在不同游戏中实现作弊功能。由于这些作弊手段需要额外硬件和复杂的设置，成本高且难以检测，普通玩家和反作弊系统很难发现。最终，作者指出，如今的作弊者面临高成本和被封禁的风险，而普通玩家很难察觉到轻微的作弊行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效检测和应对网络游戏中的作弊行为，以及作弊行为对游戏和玩家的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持实名认证和严厉惩罚**：
  - [fracus]: 提出使用统计方法或蜜罐方法检测作弊者，并认为在竞技场景中要求实名认证以确保最终责任是合理的。
  - [RALaBarge]: 认为匿名性是作弊的根源问题，提出需要极端的现实惩罚和某种中心化的身份认证机制。

• **技术性解决方案**：
  - [robertlagrant]: 建议开发一种多玩家服务器系统，限制客户端获取过多信息以防止作弊。
  - [nkrisc]: 简单指出人们为了破坏他人的乐趣而不惜一切手段，强调作弊问题的严重性。

• **作弊者心理和动机分析**：
  - [ineedasername]: 质疑作弊者的动机，特别是非竞技场景下的作弊行为，不理解为何有人会沉迷于伪装成高手。
  - [thesuitonym]: 同样不理解作弊者为何会反复使用作弊手段，认为这破坏了游戏的乐趣。

• **团队作弊和旁观者责任**：
  - [ultimafan]: 提到队友明知有人作弊却不采取行动，可能是因为从作弊中获益而不感到内疚。

43574929.article_content:
niila.fi
<- Posts
Posted: 2025-04-03
AI cheats: why you didn’t notice your teammate was cheating
For the past few years, cheats have evolved rapidly. First came memory reading aimbots, then colorbots, and now AI aim assist. Cheats have escaped the host PC. How does it affect the players and anti-cheats?
vike256
That's me, or the handle that I use online. I've been in the video game hacking scene on and off for what seems like forever. I don't know the exact point when I stumbled upon it, but I was making my first cheats on my Android phone when I was 12.
I didn't have a PC at the time, so I sat on my bed with a rooted phone in my hands that had GameGuardian installed. I remember writing a trainer with Lua for a game called Growtopia. I've since gotten a PC and programmed a few more cheats. Most notably Unibot, an open-source colorbot.
[1]
Image of Unibot debug screen while detecting an enemy. Green box is the detection area. Red box is the target.
Read more
Colorbots, why they work... or don’t
Colorbots read the enemy positions from the screen. They scan every pixel and filter based on enemy colors. It works for games that have colored enemy highlights or outlines.
Their flaw is that they don't work in every game, and they can merge multiple enemies into a single target if they are too close together. This can lock the cheater’s aim between enemies, unable to shoot either.
Image of someone having issues with multiple enemies merging into a single target. The user seems to be using Unibot.
The post
Colorbots became popular as the first cheats to achieve aimbot without memory reading. Colorbots are quite hard to detect. You can essentially just plug in a capture card to your PC and pass the images to another PC that the cheat runs on.
The aimbot input can be sent along with your normal mouse input through an Arduino or a KMBox. Just plug the KMBox to your PC and connect both the cheat PC and your mouse to it.
Diagram of how a 2PC cheat could function. This would work for both AI and colorbot cheats.
AI cheats are essentially advanced colorbots
Colorbots don't work on all games, because not all games have distinct enemy colors. This is where AI comes in. Developers train AI models to detect enemies, then distribute these models to users. This makes a single cheat work on every game imaginable.
So, the host PC only has a capture card and a "mouse" plugged into it, and the second PC runs the cheat. The anti-cheat has no idea, and...
You have no idea
You probably won’t notice the cheat while spectating, because cheat developers are intentionally nerfing their cheats to evade detection. Anti-cheats have made cheats more expensive, time-consuming, and less effective.
Today's cheats cost more but do less. Now a typical cheater needs an extra PC, external hardware, and $5-500 monthly payments just to bypass a decent anti-cheat.
After all that, they are still at a risk of getting banned. Cheaters must reflash their BIOS, wipe their PCs, reinstall Windows, and create a new account to play again. That's not something I'd like to do once a few weeks.
Cats seems to be the most helpful bunch among cheater forums.
So you being unable to spot a slight aim assist while spectating is normal. Of course you'll notice the aim assist if the player is insanely bad and has the aimbot configured wrong, but that's just plain stupidity being witnessed.
[1] Unibot is an open-source colorbot I made late 2023. It was not the first of its kind but it made waves within the cheating community. It was the first user-friendly, modifiable colorbot compatible with games like Valorant, Overwatch, and Roblox.
...yes Roblox. It has many FPS games that people play. Bad Business and Rivals are my favorites, but most people seemed to use Unibot for Arsenal. Unibot had a config file that you could use to change the important values. It was the first time users would not have to touch code to make the cheat work on their favourite game.
Unibot is still available on my GitHub. If you’re interested, check out the
GitHub Wiki
. The documentation is quite good for a game cheat.

主要讨论点：mRNA疫苗研究的联邦资助前景及相关科学问题

不同观点：
• [对研究资助受阻的担忧] ceejayoz 指出，联邦对mRNA疫苗研究的支持可能因官员的干涉而陷入危机，尤其是健康秘书Robert F. Kennedy Jr.对疫苗持反对态度，可能影响研究进展。
• [个体化治疗的疑问] tqi 提问，mRNA治疗是否需要根据个体定制靶向肽，还是具有普遍适用性。这反映了对mRNA技术在具体应用中的个性化需求缺乏了解。
• [研究内容的相关性] bookofjoe 表达了对过去发表涉及小鼠而非人类的研究文章的疑虑，提到因为经常看到评论关注“在小鼠中有效”而感到疲惫，暗示对研究成果在人类中的适用性存在担忧。

补充讨论：
• [对科学机构的质疑] pwdiscflatmajor 以讽刺语气提出“科学和美国科学促进会（AAAS）是杀手？”，可能是在质疑科学机构的动机或其对某些研究的支持。
• [临床应用的时间] fnord77 关注mRNA疫苗技术何时能进入临床应用，反映了公众对研究进展和实际医疗应用之间时间差的关注。
• [实验对象的局限性] moffkalast 简短评论“in mice”，进一步强调了许多研究仅在小鼠模型中有效，而尚未在人类中得到验证，暗示对研究成果转化到临床应用的怀疑。

争议焦点：
• 联邦资助削减和政治干预是否会实质性影响mRNA疫苗研究的进展，以及这种干预的合理性。
• mRNA技术在个体化治疗中的适用性，以及从小鼠实验到人类临床应用的转化过程中的不确定性。

data.title: Show HN: GitMCP is an automatic MCP server for every GitHub repo
data.author: liadyo
data.article_summary: GitMCP 是一个能够为任何 GitHub 项目创建远程 MCP 服务器的工具。通过将 GitHub 项目 URL 中的 "github.com" 或 "github.io" 替换为 "gitmcp.io"，用户可以为 AI 助手提供更准确的代码上下文信息，提升其回应的准确性和相关性。GitMCP 支持读取代码仓库中的文件如 llms.txt、llms-full.txt 和 readme.md，并能与 GitHub Pages 及任何公开的 GitHub 仓库无缝协作。设置简单，兼容 Claude、Cursor、Windsurf 和 VSCode Insiders 等主流 MCP 兼容的 AI 工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitMCP项目的功能、实现、应用场景及技术细节

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 对GitMCP的实际工作原理感到困惑，尤其是其具体实现和限制。他认为项目的着陆页缺乏足够的文档说明，没有解释MCP协议的具体实现细节，也没有说明如何解析和转换数据。
• [sivaragavan] 认为GitMCP项目是个好的开始，但目前实用性不强。他提到项目创建的两个工具中，一个工具未能正常工作，但另一个工具成功获取了文档。他表示对这个项目的未来可能性感兴趣。
• [ianpurton] 提供了关于LLM（大语言模型）和MCP协议如何结合使用的技术背景，解释了LLM如何通过调用函数来获取代码信息，并认为GitMCP可以在这个过程中发挥作用。
• [liadyo] 介绍了GitMCP的开源远程MCP服务器，解释了如何通过替换URL访问GitHub项目的文档，并提供了项目链接。
• [the_arun] 对GitMCP的应用场景表示不理解，质疑为什么需要为GitHub仓库设置MCP服务器。
• [pcwelder] 建议使用一个MCP服务器，通过工具调用参数来处理不同的仓库路径或URL，以减少配置的麻烦。
• [qwertox] 关注GitMCP在私有仓库和简单实现上的局限性，并建议提供Dockerfile以便于本地运行。
• [xena] 询问如何选择退出GitMCP对个人仓库的服务。
• [fzysingularity] 认为GitMCP没有充分利用MCP的状态特性，建议增强Git仓库与MCP的集成，使其更具状态性和交互性。
• [creddit] 质疑GitMCP与参考MCP服务器的区别，认为在已有参考服务器的情况下，选择自托管服务器可能不太明智。
• [eagleinparadise] 报告了在Cursor中使用GitMCP时遇到的错误，并询问是否可以强制使用MCP服务器。
• [lukew3] 对项目名称提出建议，认为当前名称可能引起混淆，建议改为更明确的描述。
• [fallat] 对MCP的快速发展表示惊讶和赞赏。
• [thomasfromcdnjs] 对项目表示赞赏和支持。

补充讨论：
• 项目的实用性和当前功能实现的有效性存在争议，部分用户认为项目尚不成熟，功能有限。
• 用户对MCP服务器在私有仓库和简单实现上的支持提出质疑，并建议改进文档和配置方式。
• 部分用户对项目的技术细节和应用场景表示困惑，尤其是MCP的具体实现和优势。
• 项目名称可能引起混淆，有用户建议更改名称以避免误解。

data.title: Show HN: Hatchet v1 – A task orchestration platform built on Postgres
data.author: abelanger
data.article_summary: Hatchet 是一个用于运行后台任务的平台，基于 Postgres 构建，帮助用户管理和分发任务，而无需自行维护任务队列或发布/订阅系统。它支持将复杂任务链组合成工作流、任务失败时发出警报、增强任务可靠性，并通过实时 web 仪表板查看任务状态。主要功能包括任务队列、任务编排（如 DAGs）、以及对任务的监控和调试支持。它适用于需要处理高负载、复杂任务逻辑以及任务可视化的场景，支持 Python、TypeScript 和 Go 等多种语言。通过 Hatchet，用户可以简化后台任务管理，提升应用的稳定性和可扩展性。

What is Hatchet?
Hatchet is a platform for running background tasks, built on top of Postgres. Instead of managing your own task queue or pub/sub system, you can use Hatchet to distribute your functions between a set of workers with minimal configuration or infrastructure.
When should I use Hatchet?
Background tasks are critical for offloading work from your main web application. Usually background tasks are sent through a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue, which helps guard against traffic spikes (queues can absorb a lot of load) and ensures that tasks are retried when your task handlers error out. Most stacks begin with a library-based queue backed by Redis or RabbitMQ (like Celery or BullMQ). But as your tasks become more complex, these queues become difficult to debug, monitor and start to fail in unexpected ways.
This is where Hatchet comes in. Hatchet is a full-featured background task management platform, with built-in support for chaining complex tasks together into workflows, alerting on failures, making tasks more durable, and viewing tasks in a real-time web dashboard.
Features
📥 Queues
Hatchet is built on a durable task queue that enqueues your tasks and sends them to your workers at a rate that your workers can handle. Hatchet will track the progress of your task and ensure that the work gets completed (or you get alerted), even if your application crashes.
This is particularly useful for:
Ensuring that you never drop a user request
Flattening large spikes in your application
Breaking large, complex logic into smaller, reusable tasks

43572733.article_summary: Hatchet 是一个用于运行后台任务的平台，基于 Postgres 构建，帮助用户管理和分发任务，而无需自行维护任务队列或发布/订阅系统。它支持将复杂任务链组合成工作流、任务失败时发出警报、增强任务可靠性，并通过实时 web 仪表板查看任务状态。主要功能包括任务队列、任务编排（如 DAGs）、以及对任务的监控和调试支持。它适用于需要处理高负载、复杂任务逻辑以及任务可视化的场景，支持 Python、TypeScript 和 Go 等多种语言。通过 Hatchet，用户可以简化后台任务管理，提升应用的稳定性和可扩展性。

data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了在个人和工作中使用AI编程工具的积极体验，尤其是在提升生产力和代码质量方面取得了显著效果。尽管一些开发者反馈AI工具效果不佳，但作者认为，经验丰富的开发者实际上能够更有效地利用这些工具。AI助手像一个拥有丰富编程知识但缺乏具体项目架构 oversight的“高级开发者”，需要开发者进行策略性指导才能发挥其最大潜力。作者提出了三个关键能力：明确的需求、工具限制和文件关键帧。他通过具体项目示例展示了AI如何自动完成整个编码过程，例如创建“平台问题监控”应用，而作者本人并不熟悉Python语言。作者建议软件开发社区应尽早接纳AI工具，以推动整个行业的发展。

• **conductr**：作为业余编程爱好者，感到LLM和生成式编程正在削弱个人创造力，造成心理上的矛盾，既觉得LLM可以提供功能性解决方案，但又因为缺乏亲手构建的满足感而感到沮丧。
• **only-one1701**：指出LLM在绿地项目（从零开始的新项目）中表现良好，但在棕地项目（已有项目的维护和扩展）中效果较差。
• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，认为可以通过“探索”方式学习新知识，并提出使用测试驱动开发（TDD）来约束和验证生成的代码，以应对LLM生成代码的不确定性。
• **rs186**：反对使用LLM生成代码，认为生成代码的调试和修正成本太高，不如自己编写代码来得省心。
• **ramoz**：认为随着AI技术的进步，高级开发者和初级开发者之间的差距会缩小，AI将对高级开发者产生威胁，并提出通过设置适当的框架，高级工程师可以更自主地使用AI。
• **yoyohello13**：对LLM持积极态度，使用Claude CLI提高工作效率，尤其在编写单元测试和处理特定任务时，认为LLM可以有效分担工作。
• **jonnycoder**：认为编写详细的提示词是使用LLM成功的关键，并提出通过创建个人应用和个人品牌来应对AI时代的挑战。
• **mmazing**：分享使用LLM的实际经验，指出LLM在处理简单算法、诊断错误和讨论潜在策略时的价值，但认为实际编码的价值在于战略性思考和减少试错。
• **denkmoon**：认为高级开发者的核心技能（如需求分析、团队协调、项目管理等）不会被LLM取代，编码只是工作中的一小部分。
• **thisdougb**：对LLM的实际应用持谨慎态度，希望看到更多实际代码案例，并对AI生成代码的质量和文档水平提出疑问。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为LLM的实际应用填补了“AI取代工作”论述中的空白，特别指出通过前期设计可以自动化大部分工作，类似于瀑布模型的复兴。
• **scandox**：怀念与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于个人和团队的成长。
• **windows2020**：认为编写代码是一种自然的放松方式，LLM并未显著提高其工作效率，编码过程中的反思和理解更为重要。
• **noodletheworld**：质疑一些文章中声称“完全没有手写代码”的说法，认为这些说法不实且令人困惑。

Introduction
Over the past few months, I have been experimenting with AI-powered coding tools in both my personal and professional projects. The experience has been overwhelmingly positive, both for me and my team of software engineers at work.
We’ve achieved better results in less time, and in many cases, the quality of our output has significantly improved.
Interestingly, this experience contrasts with the feedback I’ve received from some fellow software developers who report that AI tools aren’t working well for them.
I’m now convinced that AI-assisted software development has the potential to elevate our craft to the next level in terms of productivity. This is why I believe our community should embrace it sooner rather than later — but like all tools and practices, with the right perspective and a measured approach.
My motivation for sharing these experiences and the best practices I’ve identified is to help move the needle forward in terms of AI adoption within the broader software development community — even if realistically, it’s only by some micrometers.
The Current State of AI Coding
Beyond “Vibe Coding”
My Twitter feed suggests that AI-powered coding tools are already generating significant buzz in a specific niche: non-professional developers who are having great fun building software products. For them, these tools primarily serve as enablers, allowing them to tackle projects they might never have considered without such assistance.
More power to them — it’s exciting to witness their journey of struggles and breakthroughs.
However, this represents just one segment of potential users, and certainly not the only group for whom these tools can provide immense value.
The Senior Developer Advantage
My current conclusion, though preliminary in this rapidly evolving field, is that not only can seasoned developers benefit from this technology — they are actually in the optimal position to harness its power.
Here’s the fascinating part: The very experience and accumulated know-how in software engineering and project management — which might seem obsolete in the age of AI — are precisely what enable the most effective use of these tools.
The AI Assistant: A Senior Coder, Junior Colleague
While I haven’t found the perfect metaphor for these LLM-based programming agents in an AI-assisted coding setup, I currently think of them as “an absolute senior when it comes to programming knowledge, but an absolute junior when it comes to architectural oversight
in your specific context
.”
This means that
it takes some strategic effort to make them save you a tremendous amount of work
.
And who better to invest that effort in the right way than a senior software engineer?
As we’ll see, while we’re dealing with cutting-edge technology, it’s the time-tested, traditional practices and tools that enable us to wield this new capability most effectively.
Key Areas of Expertise
I’ve identified three critical areas of expertise needed when working with AI-assisted coding:
Well-structured Requirements
Tool-based Guard Rails
File-based Keyframing
Before diving into these concepts, let me share some real-world examples of how I’ve used AI in my projects.
I will give examples for two categories of projects: green-field and brown-field.
For both categories, I’ll focus on cases where AI handled the entire implementation, or very nearly so.
While I do sometimes use AI as a “better autocomplete” or as a chat-only companion for general discussions, this article focuses on what I call the “real deal” — where AI tooling operates in an agentic mode and handles all the heavy lifting.
Development Environment
My current tool of choice for these projects is
Cursor
, powered by Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 3.7 model. For optimal developer experience, I prefer not to manually copy-paste generated code into my codebase and need the AI assistant to execute commands directly on my local command line. Cursor provides this capability, and I expect similar products would yield comparable results.
Example 1: Platform Problem Monitoring
This setup, combined with the expertise areas I’ll discuss, enabled me to create and fully implement a green-field application:
Platform Problem Monitoring
. You can find the source code at
https://github.com/dx-tooling/platform-problem-monitoring-core
.
The application connects hourly to our ELK stack’s Elasticsearch server, reads the latest error messages, and sends us a well-formatted email summarizing the current state of problems on our web platform:
For more details, check out the
“New project: Platform Problem Monitoring”
post.
What makes this example particularly interesting is that the entire source code was written by Cursor/Claude, without any manual coding from me.
This is especially noteworthy because I don’t actually know Python. Yes, with 25+ years of software development experience, I could probably write a few lines of working Python code if pressed — but I don’t truly
know

• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，认为可以通过“探索”方式学习新知识，并提出使用测试驱动开发（TDD）来约束和验证生成的代码，以应对LLM生成代码的不确定性。
• **rs186**：反对使用LLM生成代码，认为生成代码的调试和修正成本太高，不如自己编写代码来得省心。
• **ramoz**：认为随着AI技术的进步，高级开发者和初级开发者之间的差距会缩小，AI将对高级开发者产生威胁，并提出通过设置适当的框架，高级工程师可以更自主地使用AI。
• **yoyohello13**：对LLM持积极态度，使用Claude CLI提高工作效率，尤其在编写单元测试和处理特定任务时，认为LLM可以有效分担工作。
• **jonnycoder**：认为编写详细的提示词是使用LLM成功的关键，并提出通过创建个人应用和个人品牌来应对AI时代的挑战。
• **mmazing**：分享使用LLM的实际经验，指出LLM在处理简单算法、诊断错误和讨论潜在策略时的价值，但认为实际编码的价值在于战略性思考和减少试错。
• **denkmoon**：认为高级开发者的核心技能（如需求分析、团队协调、项目管理等）不会被LLM取代，编码只是工作中的一小部分。
• **thisdougb**：对LLM的实际应用持谨慎态度，希望看到更多实际代码案例，并对AI生成代码的质量和文档水平提出疑问。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为LLM的实际应用填补了“AI取代工作”论述中的空白，特别指出通过前期设计可以自动化大部分工作，类似于瀑布模型的复兴。
• **scandox**：怀念与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于个人和团队的成长。
• **windows2020**：认为编写代码是一种自然的放松方式，LLM并未显著提高其工作效率，编码过程中的反思和理解更为重要。
• **noodletheworld**：质疑一些文章中声称“完全没有手写代码”的说法，认为这些说法不实且令人困惑。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：LLM生成代码的质量和实用性是主要争议点，一些开发者认为其生成的代码质量低，调试成本高，而另一些开发者则认为通过适当的方法和工具，LLM可以有效提高工作效率。
• **心理影响**：部分开发者（如conductr）感到LLM削弱了他们的创造力和满足感，而另一些开发者（如yoyohello13和mmazing）则认为LLM可以有效分担工作，提高效率。
• **高级开发者的角色**：一些观点（如denkmoon和ramoz）认为高级开发者的核心技能不会被LLM取代，但也有观点（如ramoz）认为AI将对高级开发者产生威胁。
• **实际应用**：讨论中涉及了LLM在绿地项目和棕地项目中的不同表现，以及通过TDD和框架设置来约束和验证生成代码的方法。

data.title: How Big Is VMS? – VMS Software, Inc
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了VMS操作系统的大小，特别是其源代码的行数。作者通过自定义程序统计了VMS多个版本（V6.2、V7.2、V8.2、V9.2-3）中15个核心组件的源代码行数，排除了空白行和注释行。结果显示，这15个组件在V8.2版本中总计约16.6万行代码，且这些组件的代码量在不同版本中几乎翻了三倍。VMS最初使用BLISS和MACRO-32编写，后来逐步转向C语言。每个新版本大约增加40万行代码，显示出VMS在不断发展和扩展。文章还提到，VMS源代码库包含409个组件，大小不一，共同构成了多平台的VMS操作系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VMS操作系统的当前价值和历史演变

不同观点：
• jamesy0ung认为VMS今天的主要用途仅限于那些无法迁移的现有应用。他对VMS的可靠性有所耳闻，但对其一年期的VM许可感到不满，认为VMS已经过时且小众，不如Linux等主流系统实用，因为Linux有众多厂商支持。

• markus_zhang对VMS的设计者David Cutler表示钦佩，并提到Cutler在微软的工作经历，表达了对与Cutler共事的向往。

• snovymgodym对VMS持负面看法，认为其历史是一连串的错误决策，错失市场机会，并最终成为遗留软件，仅用于从某些机构中榨取最后的价值。不过，他仍希望VMS能有一天被开源。

• uptownfunk对VMS怀有情感，提到VMS相关技术（如VAX）曾为他们家庭带来生计，因此对VMS有深厚感情，不论其多么过时。

• whartung对VMS代码库中ACPI部分的代码行数（超过165K行）感到惊讶，虽然他并不熟悉ACPI的细节，但觉得这个数字很大。

• zabzonk请求澄清讨论的VMS版本是否为VAX VMS。

• ConanRus对VMS的知识产权持有者表示不满，认为他们没有有效管理这一遗产，尤其在开源社区贡献方面缺乏支持，并提到因过时的VM映像下载机制导致用户不便。

补充讨论：
• VMS的历史演变和市场表现是多个评论者关注的焦点，尤其是其错失技术发展机会（如Alpha和Itanium架构）导致当前的尴尬局面。
• VMS的可靠性和其在特定领域中的应用仍然被一些用户所认可，尽管其市场影响已经大不如前。
• 开源和用户友好性是部分评论者对VMS现状的批评点，尤其是对旧有系统如何在现代技术环境中生存和发展的关注。

43573738.article_content:
How Big Is VMS?
This question was asked during my Boot Camp presentation last fall in Boston, and over the past 35 years dozens of times people have asked, how big is VMS? That translates into "how many lines of code are in VMS"? I thought it was time to at least make a stab at pursuing some insight into the answer. I wrote some command procedures to count the number of source lines in .B32, .B64, .C, .MAR, .M64, and .S files. Not counted are blank lines and lines beginning with the standard comment characters and miscellaneous directives for the particular language.
First, I needed a baseline definition of  'VMS'.
Does it include layered products, networking, compilers, RTLs, debuggers, open source, etc.?
Is it the code on a particular running system?
Does it include command procedures?
I said 'no' to all of the above and as a starting point chose 15 facilities which are representative of identifiable components of the system: ACPI , AUDSRV, CLUSTER, DCL, DRIVER, F11X, JOBCTL, LAN, PCSI, RMS, SCSI, SDA, SHADOWING, SYS, XFC.
I chose the following releases for comparison:
V6.2:       May / 1995 - port to Alpha
V7.2:       Feb / 1999 - kernel threads, 64-bit APIs, Galaxy, and more
V8.2:       Feb /  2005 - port to Itanium
V9.2-3:     Dec / 2024 - port to x86
The LINES.COM procedure, which invokes a set of nested procedures, fetches all of the source files with the extensions mentioned above, in the SCSI facility that are in the release stream V8.2, gets the line counts, and produces the text file below. This was done for each of the 15 facilities in each of the four release streams.
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ @lines scsi "V8.2" V82
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ type [.scsi]total-line-counts-v82.txt
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.BLISS]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 2
Total source lines = 7770
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.C]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 64
Total source lines = 119609
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.M64]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 1
Total source lines = 885
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.MAR]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 34
Total source lines = 38414
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.S]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 0
Total source lines = 0
Grand Totals
Total source files = 101
Total source lines = 166678
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$
Here are all the totals for V8.2. There is a similar chart for each of the other three releases.
Here is the lines of code summary for the four releases. You can find a graphical representation of the table below at this
link
.
Notes and Observations:
Not all code in a facility is in every release, but it is or has been in one or more releases.
There are 409 facilities in the VMS source pool - some big, some small. They contribute to the VMS operating system build for one or more platforms.
These 15 facilities chosen comprise close to two million lines of code and their total has nearly tripled in size during the last three releases.
There were many changes and additions to VMS between V8.2 and V9.2-3 prior to the x86 porting work.
Given a relatively small delta, each release has increased by about 400,000 lines of code.
The emergence of C code is another aspect of VMS that is part of the story. In the beginning, VMS was written in BLISS and MACRO-32 (VAX assembler). During the latter stages of the port to Alpha, we declared that all new code would be written in C. There are exceptions, of course, but for the most part we followed this guideline. Not shown in the data above, but part of this investigation, is the following which reflects the 15 facilities. (The 31 C modules in V6.2 were all written during the port to Alpha.)
It might be interesting to look into why some facilities have changed so much over time. Some seem obvious but others do not. If you have suggestions for a future post, please speak up.
Mar 31st, 2025
Clair Grant
VMS Researcher

data.title: A university president makes a case against cowardice
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年，美国高等教育面临严峻挑战，特朗普第二任政府对高校的多样性、公平和包容努力展开调查，削减联邦资金，并驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学因联邦政府压力，同意改变政策，随后获得资金恢复，但其校长随后辞职。许多高校领导因担心职位和预算而不愿公开反对政府政策，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯是个例外。罗斯自2007年起担任校长，积极发表文章，呼吁高校坚持原则。2023年，韦斯利安大学因最高法院裁决终止了传承录取政策。罗斯支持言论自由，并在加沙战争抗议中与学生发生冲突。他批评其他高校领导采用1967年芝加哥大学的《卡尔文报告》中的中立原则，认为这不过是避免麻烦的借口。面对特朗普政府对学术界的攻击，罗斯持续发声，敦促同行捍卫原则。在与作者的对话中，罗斯表示现实比他预期的更糟糕，许多高校不愿公开支持非党派活动，显示出对参与公共事务的犹豫。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对美国大学系统及其当前争议的看法

不同观点：
• **支持大学管理层的立场**：necubi认为，Wesleyan大学校长Roth在平衡言论自由和提供安全学习环境方面表现得非常深思熟虑。他坚持不屈服于抗议者的无限制要求，同时捍卫他们抗议的权利。这种立场在2020年后尤为重要，因为大学面临来自不同政治光谱的压力。

• **对大学种族考虑的批评**：rahimnathwani指出，Wesleyan大学在招生过程中考虑种族因素，并为此在法律案件中辩护，这与自由民主的原则相悖。他认为，如果大学坚持这种做法，就不应获得任何形式的纳税人资助。

• **对捐赠者和财富影响的担忧**：mmooss提到，超级富豪正在形成一个主导阶层，影响大学的自由和民主。他质疑这些财富是否在攻击大学自由，并指出某些事件（如哈佛领导层的退出）可能与此相关。

• **反制措施的建议**：siliconc0w建议大学可以通过拒绝录取持有反教育政策的学生来捍卫其价值观。这种激进的做法旨在维护大学的教育使命。

• **公众对大学敌意的原因**：sequoia提出，为什么许多人对大学怀有敌意，是否大学在过去几十年中可以采取不同做法以获得更广泛的同情。这个问题引发了对公众态度是否完全非理性的讨论。

• **政府资金与大学自主权的关系**：carbocation和trentnix都提到，大学是否接受政府资金与其自主权之间的关系。接受政府资金可能导致大学在政策上受到政治影响。

• **对大学失去道德高地的批评**：CSMastermind认为，大学因 prioritize 意识形态高于真理追求、重视身份高于卓越、排斥政治外人士而失去了道德高地和观点多样性。

• **减少政府参与的建议**：guywithahat和mmooss建议，大学应减少对政府资金的依赖，通过竞争获得学生和研究资金，避免政治对学术的过度影响。

补充讨论：
• **对现代激进主义的反思**：一些评论（如rahimnathwani和mantas）批评了大学在激进主义和言论自由方面的双重标准，指出某些激进主义实际上是在压制不喜欢的观点。

• **历史与现代抗议的比较**：JacobiX提到现代抗议与越战时期抗议的历史相似性，引发对两者异同的思考。

争议焦点：
• 大学在招生和治理过程中考虑种族因素的正当性。
• 大学是否应减少对政府资金的依赖以维护其自主权。
• 公众对大学敌意的根本原因及其合理性。

总体而言，讨论围绕大学自由、言论自由、种族政策以及政府和财富对大学的影响展开，反映了当前社会对高等教育机构的多方面争议。

Last Friday could have passed for a lovely spring day on the Connecticut campus of Wesleyan University. Students with books and laptops dotted a green hillside; flocks of admissions visitors trailed tour guides; baseball season had just begun, and practice was under way. It was almost possible to forget the grim straits of American higher education in 2025.
Colleges and universities have been early targets of the second Trump Administration. In the past month, the Administration has announced it will investigate diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts at more than fifty schools; cut hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding from such institutions as Johns Hopkins and the University of Pennsylvania; and sought to deport international students involved in pro-Palestinian activism. Columbia received a letter from the federal government issuing demands—which included making changes to discipline and admission policies, and placing the department of Middle East, South Asian, and African Studies under “academic receivership”—to be met as a “precondition” for negotiating the restoration of four hundred million dollars in federal funding. The university agreed to these demands the following week; the week after that, the university’s president resigned.
Columbia’s capitulation was in line with a general trend toward circumspection. The memory of Congress grilling university presidents in 2023 seems to be fresh among leaders in higher ed: few want to risk either their jobs or their budgets by saying the wrong thing. A handful of exceptions have stood out; for example, President Christopher Eisgruber, of Princeton, who wrote a piece for
The Atlantic
about “
The Cost of the Government’s Attack on Columbia
.” (This week, the Administration suspended dozens of grants to Princeton.) But perhaps none has been as voluble or persistent as Michael Roth, who has been president of Wesleyan since 2007.
Roth is a historian and a Wesleyan alumnus who, as an undergraduate, designed a major in the history of psychological theory. His scholarship has dealt with Freud and memory but also colleges as institutions, in books such as “
Safe Enough Spaces
” (2019) and “
The Student: A Short History
” (2023). Recent years have brought an increasingly political thrust to both his writing (for national media and his
presidential blog
) and to his work as president. In 2023, in response to the Supreme Court’s ruling against affirmative action, Wesleyan ended legacy admissions.
When Wesleyan students joined the national wave of protests over the war on Gaza, Roth—who describes himself as a supporter of both free speech and Israel’s right to exist—tangled with student protesters as well as with those who wanted him to shut the protests down. Meanwhile, in interviews and essays, he took administrators at other colleges to task for embracing the principles like those found in the “
Kalven report
”—a 1967 document out of the University of Chicago, which advanced the argument that universities should almost always remain scrupulously neutral. (Such stances were, he told me, “a cover for trying to stay out of trouble.”) As the Trump Administration has ramped up its attacks on the academy, Roth has continued to publish widely, urging fellow-leaders to stand up for their principles. “Release Mahmoud Khalil! Respect freedom of speech!” he concluded in
a recent column for
Slate
, which argued that the Columbia activist’s arrest “should terrify every college president.”
Roth and I met in his office, which is dominated by a round  table where he meets with both students and his cabinet. Wearing Blundstones and polka-dot socks, he was loose-limbed and gregarious, and our conversation (which has been edited for length and clarity) was punctuated by the bright sound of batting from the baseball diamond just outside.
You wrote last year, before the election, that colleges and universities weren’t ready for what was coming. How has the reality compared to your expectations?
It’s much worse than I expected.
I had this idea—alas, it was in 2020, just as
COVID
was happening—that it would be great if colleges and universities took our civic responsibilities more seriously and really incentivized students to participate in the public sphere: work on a campaign, zoning commission, whatever. Rigorously agnostic about what they chose to work on. We found a few hundred schools that agreed in principle and we created a network. Before the 2024 election, we reactivated that group, and this time around, the institutions were much less likely to want to be publicly in support of even something so nonpartisan.
We’re really small—three thousand students or so—and I wanted University of Texas at Austin, and Michigan, other big places. Some of them did agree in principle, but this time, in 2024—in the spring, let’s say, when Biden was still in the race, it was clear Trump was going to be the candidate—th

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：伺服电机的技术原理、实际应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [viraptor] 认为文章没有深入解释伺服电机的工作原理。他指出，文章只介绍了控制信号和伺服电机的响应结果，但缺少脉冲如何被转换、反馈机制如何工作以及安全机制等关键技术细节。

• [arbitrandomuser] 分享了一个黑客改造的视频链接，展示了如何让玩具伺服电机具有更高的精度和可重复性，但没有详细讨论技术细节。

• [Animats] 提到文章讨论的是1970年代的无线电控制玩具伺服电机，指出这些早期设备缺乏反馈输出，但仍然在低端机械输出设备中占主导地位，语气中带有不满。

• [dcrazy] 对电子元件分销商（如Jameco、Mouser等）提供大量入门教育文章的现象表示疑惑，推测这可能是为了SEO（搜索引擎优化），但同时质疑在这样一个相对小众的领域是否有必要这样做。

• [bilsbie] 提出一个基础问题，询问伺服电机如何保持其位置，以及这是否需要能量，关注的是电机工作的基本原理。

• [mkarliner] 对文章内容的真实性提出质疑，怀疑文章可能是由AI生成的。

• [brcmthrowaway] 分享了自己使用 hobby 伺服电机的实际体验，提到该电机产生高分贝的刺耳噪音，并询问有哪些更好的伺服电机选择。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术细节包括伺服电机的工作原理、反馈机制和安全机制，部分用户（如viraptor）对这些内容的缺失表示不满。
• 实际应用中的问题也被提及，例如伺服电机的噪音问题（brcmthrowaway）以及低端设备在市场中的持续存在（Animats）。
• 关于文章本身的质疑（mkarliner）和分销商SEO策略的讨论（dcrazy）为次要讨论点，但仍具有一定参考价值。

data.title: Show HN: Monkeys.zip – 3000 Monkeys on Typewriters
data.author: yathern
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个可定制猴子工作环境的在线项目的评论，涉及功能、技术实现、用户体验、潜在的商业模式以及技术问题等方面。

不同观点：
• [netsharc] 调侃该项目可以通过售卖虚拟物品（如"monkeycoins"）来盈利，用户可以购买定制物品。这暗示了对可能商业模式的幽默批评。
• [voussoir] 对项目的动画和整体表现给予高度评价，特别赞赏其中的个性化表现。
• [h1fra] 指出了技术问题，包括登录后无法获得猴子、页面需要手动刷新以及特定页面无法访问等问题，强调了用户体验中的技术故障。
• [mechagodzilla] 分享了自己过去类似的编程经历，增加了一个技术背景下的趣闻，但没有直接评价该项目的好坏。
• [hombre_fatal] 对项目的高度完成度表示惊讶，并表示对技术实现细节感兴趣，倾向于进一步了解技术层面。
• [sen] 喜欢项目的可爱设计和互动性，但提出希望增加从“单词视图”返回“猴子视图”的功能，以提升用户体验。
• [vekatimest] 质疑该项目是否计划通过付费道具和认领功能来盈利，将其与三年前的NFT项目相比较，表达了对商业化的担忧。
• [Spacemolte] 指出在缩放时看到了不合适的符号（如纳粹十字），这是一个严重的视觉问题。
• [chewmieser] 提出功能建议，包括去除1-2个字符的单词以及修复iOS上无法滚动的问题，展现了对改进项目的建设性态度。
• [BugsJustFindMe] 开玩笑说许多猴子看起来像猿而不是猴子，指出设计上的不准确。
• [lugvruzzle] 提到登录功能存在问题，特别是使用电子邮件登录时，关注用户体验中的技术问题。
• [thomasfromcdnjs] 对项目的渲染表示赞赏，并请求提供更多技术细节，展现了对技术实现的浓厚兴趣。
• [krzat] 对项目能否生成有意义的句子表示好奇，关注项目的长期效果。
• [yeah879846] 对项目能否生成莎士比亚作品表示怀疑，质疑项目的实际能力。
• [ChrisArchitect] 以讽刺的方式提问如何搜索特定猴子写的单词，暗示了对项目功能的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 项目在技术实现和动画表现上获得了赞赏，但也有用户指出登录问题、页面故障和技术故障等需要修复的问题。
• 商业模式方面，有用户对项目可能的付费功能和盈利模式表示担忧，并将其与过去的NFT项目相比较。
• 部分用户对项目的设计细节提出了建议，如单词过滤和导航功能的改进，以提升用户体验。
• 个别用户对项目能否实现其声称的长远目标（如生成莎士比亚作品）表示怀疑。

data.title: The Slow Collapse of Critical Thinking in OSINT Due to AI
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了开源情报（OSINT）领域中由于生成式人工智能（GenAI）工具的广泛使用，分析师的批判性思维能力逐渐减弱的问题。作者Nico Dekens指出，过去OSINT强调思维分析，但现在越来越多的人依赖AI完成任务，如总结文档、翻译文本、生成报告等，导致分析师的批判性思考和验证工作减少。研究表明，对AI的信任增加会降低用户的批判性思维，使他们更少质疑和验证信息。文章警告，过度依赖AI可能使OSINT从业者失去判断力与专业 integrity，从调查者变为自动化操作者。文章呼吁业内人士重拾批判性思维，避免在AI辅助下失去思考能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）工具（如生成型AI）在工作流程中的影响，尤其是对批判性思维和信息验证的影响。

不同观点：
• **BrenBarn**：认为文章虽然声称不是对AI的抱怨，但实际上提出了严重的警示。他将AI的使用比作毒品成瘾，指出免费向所有人分发AI工具可能带来风险，因为这种方式容易导致人们依赖AI而不再自主思考。
• **Aurornis**：反驳关于AI让人变得懒惰的观点，认为那些依赖AI的人之前也依赖其他媒体（如播客、新闻、社交媒体），AI只是提供了更便捷的意见来源。AI用户和沉迷于TikTok视频以获取知识的人没有本质区别。
• **0hijinks**：质疑AI在研究和发现任务中的有效性，指出如果用户必须对AI的答案进行详细验证，那还不如自己从头做起。他怀疑使用AI是否真的能提高效率。
• **jruohonen**：同意文章的观点，指出人们在使用AI时确实减少了批判性思考，例如不再形成假设、验证来源和评估多个视角，这种情况已经在实际工作流程中出现。
• **sepositus**：质疑专业人士因为AI的快速、自信和清晰的回答而停止批判性思考的说法，认为如果专业人士没有研究AI的局限性，那就是懒惰。
• **treyfitty**：支持AI工具的实用性，例如在查询基本信息时，AI可以快速提供答案，减少不必要的努力。
• **tqi**：对文章中关于AI导致批判性思维崩溃的预测表示怀疑，认为这可能是作者的确认偏误，而不是理性分析的结果。
• **roenxi**：文章没有讨论AI对分析质量的影响，指出AI虽然不像类型检查器那样绝对正确，但在某些方面可能比人类平均水平要好。他认为AI的影响不一定是负面的。

补充讨论：
• **palmotea**：指出AI的广泛适用性，认为文章讨论的问题不仅限于开放源情报（OSINT）领域，而是在所有采用AI工具的领域都存在。
• **pcj-github**：分享了个人经验，指出AI在学习新技能时虽然能降低入门门槛，但可能延缓深入掌握技能的过程，因为用户容易依赖AI进行思考。
• **BariumBlue**：提到AI的自信语气容易让人误以为其答案准确，这是用户需要注意的问题。
• **zora_goron**：提出“人类->AI推理转移”的概念，指出AI工具在帮助完成非推理任务时也可能悄然影响人类的推理过程，因为AI决定了哪些信息重要。
• **Barrin92**：质疑专业分析师的专业性，认为如果连基本的分析能力（如区分巴黎和比利时）都需要AI帮助，那是令人担忧的。他批评文章没有深入探讨信息验证和批判性思考的基本要求。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是否导致用户减少批判性思考和自主验证。

The Slow Collapse of Critical Thinking in OSINT due to AI
Nico Dekens | dutch_osintguy
19 hours ago
9 min read
OSINT used to be a thinking game. Now it’s becoming a trusting game and that should terrify you.
I’ve seen it firsthand, analysts running solid investigations, then slowly shifting more and more of the thinking to GenAI tools. At first, it’s small. You use ChatGPT to summarise a document or translate a foreign post. Then it’s helping draft your reports. Then it’s generating leads. And eventually, you’re not thinking as critically as you used to. You’re verifying less, questioning less, relying more.
We tell ourselves we’re “working smarter.” But somewhere along the way, we stop noticing how much of the actual thinking is being offloaded.
This isn’t a rant against AI. I use it daily, ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Gemini. They’re in my workflow like everyone else’s. But the tradecraft is slipping. Analysts are skipping the hard parts. They’re trusting GenAI to do the heavy cognitive lifting, and it’s changing how we operate at a foundational level.
When OSINT becomes too easy, too efficient, too comfortable… you should be worried. Tradecraft isn’t just about speed, it’s about judgment. And judgment doesn’t come from a language model. If we keep going down this path without pushing back, without actively preserving the critical habits that define our profession, we risk becoming operators of automation instead of investigators.
This blog is a wake-up call. For myself. For anyone working in OSINT. For the people teaching it, and the people just getting started. If we don’t reclaim the thinking side of this game, we’ll lose the game entirely.
The Study That Should Alarm You
In early 2025, a team from Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft Research published something every OSINT analyst should read, but most haven’t. It was a large-scale survey of 319 knowledge workers using GenAI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, and Gemini in their daily work.
What they found is a warning shot.
The study revealed a clear pattern: the more confidence users had in the AI, the less they thought critically. In contrast, the more confident they were in themselves, the more likely they were to question the output, verify the information, and think deeply about the task.
Let that sink in: Confidence in AI replaces confidence in self and with it, the thinking disappears.
Here’s the punchline:
High trust in GenAI consistently led to reduced critical thinking and less cognitive effort across the board.
Participants weren’t lazy. They were experienced professionals. But when the tool responded quickly, confidently, and clearly they stopped doing the hard part. They stopped questioning. Stopped verifying. Stopped applying the mental friction that separates automation from investigation.
The scary part is that many users still believed they were thinking critically, because GenAI made them feel smart.
The researchers saw a new type of behavior emerge:
•  Instead of forming hypotheses, users asked the AI for ideas.
•  Instead of validating sources, they assumed the AI had already done so.
•  Instead of assessing multiple perspectives, they integrated and edited the AI’s summary and moved on.
This isn’t hypothetical. This is happening now, in real-world workflows. And if you’re in OSINT, you know how dangerous that is.
In our line of work, you can’t afford false confidence. You can’t afford a hallucinated source, a mistranslated post, or a manipulated summary. But the more trust you place in GenAI, without friction, without skepticism, the more you risk exactly that.
The study didn’t focus on OSINT directly. But it doesn’t have to. The findings hit home harder here than anywhere else. Because if we lose critical thinking in this field, we don’t just lose accuracy, we lose integrity.
What This Means for OSINT
In OSINT, we deal in fragments. Nothing is handed to us neatly. We build context from chaos:   tweets, photos, forums, leaks, metadata, satellite images, dead links, weird file names. Every good analyst knows that the work isn’t just collecting data. It’s thinking with it.
That’s what’s at risk.
The
Lee et al. study
wasn’t about OSINT specifically, but it described exactly what’s happening in OSINT shops, government teams, threat intel units, and open-source communities around the world. The creeping shift from thinking to prompting, from analyst to editor. Let’s talk real.
Real-World OSINT Scenarios Affected by GenAI Complacency
Scenario 1: Image Verification
You upload a protest photo into a tool like Gemini and ask, “Where was this taken?” It spits out a convincing response: “Paris, near Place de la République.” It sounds right. You move on.
But a trained eye would notice the signage is Belgian. The license plates are off. The architecture doesn’t match. You trusted the AI and missed the location by a country.

You use Claude to summarize a person’s online presence. It generates a clean narr

data.author: kiwicopple
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了声明式 schema 如何简化复杂数据库的管理。声明式 schema 将数据库的最终期望状态存储在 `.sql` 文件中，便于集中管理和版本控制。相比直接修改数据库 schema，声明式 schema 具有以下优势：单一管理界面，减少冗余和错误；版本化迁移，确保不同环境中的一致性；简明的代码审查，无需重复复杂迁移脚本。

随着数据库 schema 复杂性增加，传统迁移方法难以维护，因为缺乏单一的整体视图。例如，在 Supabase 中，复杂的 `projects` 表涉及私有表、RLS（行级安全）、视图和触发器，修改时需多步操作，容易导致冲突。

声明式 schema 通过集中管理 schema，简化了开发流程，提高了开发效率。

Declarative Schemas for Simpler Database Management
03 Apr 2025
•
7 minute read
Qiao Han
Engineering
Today we’re releasing declarative schemas to simplify managing and maintaining complex database schemas. With declarative schemas, you can define your database structure in a clear, centralized, and version-controlled manner.
What are declarative schemas?
#
Declarative schemas store the final desired state of the database in
.sql
files that can be saved and versioned alongside a project. For example, here is the declarative schema for a classic
products
table:
_
10
create table "products" (
_
10
"id" serial primary key,
_
10
"name" text not null,
_
10
"description" text,
_
10
"price" numeric(10,2) not null,
_
10
"created_at" timestamp default now()
_
10
);
_
10
_
10
alter table "products"
_
10
enable row level security;
Declarative schemas offer numerous benefits over making changes to your database schema directly:
Single pane of glass
. Maintain your entire database schema in one place, reducing redundancy and potential errors.
Versioned migrations
. Automatically generate migration files, ensuring consistent schema updated across environments. Store your declarative schema files alongside your project files in your version control system.
Concise code reviews
. Easily review changes to tables, views, and functions without manually repeating complex migration scripts.
Declarative schemas vs migrations
#
It's best practice to use
Migrations
to track and apply changes to databases. Every time you make a change, you create a new new file with all the changes, keeping changes versioned and reproducible.
However, as the complexity of a database schemas grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to develop using versioned migrations as there isn't a single place to see the entire database schema.
For example, at Supabase we have a complex and frequently-updated
projects
table. Here's partially what it looks like with RLS enabled:
_
32
create table private.projects (
_
32
id              bigint    not null,
_
32
name            text      not null,
_
32
organization_id bigint    not null,
_
32
inserted_at     timestamp not null,
_
32
updated_at      timestamp not null
_
32
);
_
32
_
32
alter table private.projects
_
32
enable row level security;
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_insert
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for insert
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
with check auth.can_write(project_id);
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_select
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for select
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
using auth.can_read(project_id);
_
32
_
32
-- Users can only view the projects that they have access to
_
32
create view public.projects as select
_
32
projects.id,
_
32
projects.name,
_
32
projects.organization_id,
_
32
projects.inserted_at,
_
32
projects.updated_at
_
32
from private.projects
_
32
where auth.can_read(projects.id);
The
projects
table is created in a private schema, with a public view exposed for reads. Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is implemented on top of RLS policies to ensure queries only return projects that the user has access to.
Since Postgres views are not updatable by default, we have defined trigger functions to cascade writes to the underlying table when a Supabase user creates a new project. This makes development easier because the
projects
view can be inserted with regular PostgREST calls while invoking the appropriate RLS policies on the underlying table.
_
24
-- Triggers to update views from PostgREST: select('projects').insert({ ... })
_
24
create function public.public_projects_on_insert() returns trigger
_
24
as $$
_
24
begin
_
24
insert into private.projects(
_
24
name,
_
24
organization_id,
_
24
inserted_at,
_
24
updated_at
_
24
) values (
_
24
NEW.name,
_
24
NEW.organization_id,
_
24
coalesce(NEW.inserted_at, now()),
_
24
coalesce(NEW.updated_at, now())
_
24
) returning * into NEW;
_
24
return NEW;
_
24
end
_
24
$$ language plpgsql;
_
24
_
24
create trigger public_projects_on_insert
_
24
instead of insert
_
24
on public.projects
_
24
for each row
_
24
execute function public.public_projects_on_insert();
This complexity slows down development velocity, as changes to the table might break other views or functions. Back in early 2022, a simple change to add a new column involved the following steps.
Find the latest schema for
projects
table in our migration files or by querying our database.
Write the
alter table
statement in a new migration file.
Copy and update the
projects
view definition to include the new column.
Copy and update the trigger function definition to include the new column.
Add new pgTAP tests and verify that existing tests pass.
Submit the new migration file for review, which would be at least a few hundred lines.
This process is tedious and it's frustrating to have multiple engineers working on the
projects
table concurrently. Merging PRs would result in a merge conflict that must be resolved by repeating steps 1-5.

data.title: Celebrate 50 years of Microsoft with the company's original source code
data.author: EvgeniyZh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕GW-BASIC源代码及其历史背景的讨论

不同观点：
• stkai和zabzonk等人赞赏GW-BASIC源代码的质量和历史意义，特别是其中有趣的注释以及当年技术实现的难度。stkai引用了源代码中的幽默注释，zabzonk则通过分享自己用FORTRAN77编写Intel 8080模拟器的经历，表达了对早期技术成就的钦佩。
• billforsternz批评了网站的用户体验，认为其动画设计过于花哨，不符合1970年代的技术风格，建议使用更简洁、轻量的技术来呈现信息。
• winrid和jer0me则对网页设计和源代码的展示形式提出意见，winrid开玩笑说网站错过了使用win98.css的机会，jer0me提供了源代码的链接，并提醒文件大小为100 MB。

补充讨论：
• 关于源代码的法律风险，switch007开玩笑地提到阅读源代码可能会引发法律诉讼，反映了人们对代码泄露事件的敏感性。
• 对微软及比尔·盖茨的评价存在分歧，santiagobasulto指出尽管微软在黑客社区中不受欢迎，但盖茨和艾伦对技术发展的贡献不可否认。rayiner则对微软的市场成功持批评态度，认为其成功与实际技术能力不符。
• 技术实现的历史细节引发了讨论，starik36好奇当年源代码是如何输入到Altair计算机中的，是否需要重新输入或通过某种早期的存储介质。
• 其他如froggertoaster和Seanambers的评论较为个人化，前者提到与比尔·盖茨的短暂会面，后者则批评文章对读者的技术水平定位不准。

争议焦点：
• 网站设计是否应更贴近1970年代的真实体验，以及微软及比尔·盖茨在技术历史中的地位评价。

data.title: Supervisors often prefer rule breakers, up to a point
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：规则的制定目的、遵守与打破的合理性以及在不同情境下的处理方式

不同观点：
• 一些评论者认为理解规则制定的背景和目的至关重要，并强调在确保规则制定者会满意的情况下，可以灵活应对规则。例如，[seeknotfind]指出应理解规则的制定原因并确保规则制定者会满意。[yi_xuan]也强调理解规则的目的和影响是关键。

• 另一些评论者指出规则往往是简化的，以适应复杂的情况，因此可能限制了一些好的行为而允许了一些坏的行为。例如，[pdpi]认为简单的规则在复杂情况下不可避免地会有妥协，存在“允许的坏行为”和“禁止的好行为”的空间。[taeric]进一步指出，有目的性地打破规则并不一定是坏事，但需要在主管可接受的范围内。

• 部分评论者分享了实际管理经验，表示更倾向于信任员工的判断和内在动机，而不是严格执行规则。例如，[madrox]提到除非员工表现不佳，否则不会严格执行考勤政策。[jbmsf]则认为制定规则主要是为了防止最坏的情况发生，对于不属于“最坏的人”的员工会有一定的灵活性。

• 还有一些评论者讨论了规则的起源和组织对规则的重视程度对规则打破的影响。例如，[neilv]提出了规则的来源、组织对规则的重视程度以及管理者与组织在规则上的 alignment 等问题，认为这些因素会影响规则打破的合理性和后果。[nitwit005]特别指出在体育界，员工可能被指示去打破联赛规则而不是公司规则。

• 其他一些评论者从实际操作和风险角度讨论了规则打破的利弊。例如，[userbinator]认为规则打破者能带来收益并移除责任。[rblatz]和[ungreased0675]分享了关于体育界中实际案例的观察，指出某些不当行为可能因其带来的控制力和好处而被默许。[terramars]则通过具体例子说明了规则打破在不同领域（如体育和商业）中的不同影响。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者提到规则打破的文化差异，例如[userbinator]引用了“先行动后求谅解”的俗语，而[jvanderbot]则指出管理者可以通过责备规则打破者并从中获得好处。

• 最后，[__turbobrew__]强调了使命聚焦的重要性，认为理解组织的目标和运作方式是决定何时打破规则的关键。

争议的焦点主要在于规则打破的合理性和后果，尤其是在不同情境和组织文化下的适用性。

data.title: The cultural evolution of distortion in music
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： distortion（失真）在音乐中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• Tade0认为，电吉他失真的波形通常接近锯齿波，而不是三角波，除非弦在正中拨动。他还提到失真的音色会根据弹奏技巧和设备的不同而变化，例如不同放大器（如Mesa Boogie）和效果器（如BOSS DS-1）如何通过技术限制产生独特的音色。Tade0还强调了失真在动态和音色变化中的作用。

• Kazinator指出，单音失真（如电吉他独奏）在主流音乐中较快被接受，因为电路技术不断改进。然而，过于刺耳的失真音色仍然是小众的，只在特定音乐风格中（如重金属）得到广泛应用。他还讨论了失真如何影响和声结构，特别是在重金属音乐中通过失真创造出复杂的音调关系。

• Driggs对原文的长篇分析持批评态度，认为其过于学术化，缺乏艺术性表达。Driggs更欣赏如Henry Rollins和Don Was之间的对话，这种更直接、贴近艺术本身的讨论。

• Myself248分享了个人经历，通过播放Pink Floyd的音乐向他人解释失真，并提出了一个理论，即失真吉他声音类似于发动机的声音，象征着自由，这可能是年轻人被摇滚乐吸引的原因之一。

• Drops引用了Brian Eno的话，强调失真是媒介超越其承载能力的标志，是“失败的声音”，这种声音最终会被珍惜和模仿。Drops的观点强调了失真在现代艺术中作为一种突破媒介限制的表现形式。

补充讨论：
• 失真在不同音乐风格中的接受度和应用方式不同，尤其是重金属和爵士/摇滚融合音乐中失真的使用差异。
• 失真音色的变化与设备的技术限制和演奏技巧密切相关，如放大器和效果器的设计如何影响音色。
• 失真作为艺术表现的一部分，其美学价值和象征意义被不同评论者从个人经历和哲学角度进行了探讨。

data.title: Binary Distribution Rebuilds
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: 本文总结了作者在重建Debian和Ubuntu软件包（amd和arm64架构）方面的实验，并与新推出的Reproduce.Debian.net项目进行比较。作者的实验使用最新版软件包进行重建，而Reproduce.Debian.net则使用与发布包相同的构建输入以实现更高的可重现性。作者指出，虽然Reproduce.Debian.net有可能达到100%的可重现性，但还需更进一步，实现“幂等重建”（Idempotent Rebuild），即通过反复重建最终得到一致的档案。当前，由于时间戳和不确定输出等问题，N（重建次数）可能为无穷大，但理想情况是实现N=1。作者计划发布阶段#0的构建产物以进一步实验，但目前尚未取得更多技术进展。

主要讨论点：Debian main 是否能够自我重建以及如何解决其中涉及的非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的问题。

不同观点：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 认为 Debian main 可能已经进入了一种无法自我重建的状态，主要因为非自由固件和未由 Debian 签名的二进制文件的存在。这些因素可能破坏了 Debian 的可重建性和纯粹性。他提出，如果没有任何非自由包被用作构建输入，可以通过在一个没有 blob（非自由固件）的平台上引导 Guix，并从那里交叉构建 Debian。

• [lrvick] 提供了另一种思路，建议考虑使用具有更严格供应链安全策略的工具，如 Guix，并推荐了 https://stagex.tools/ 作为替代方案，以应对 Debian 目前可能面临的供应链安全问题。

补充讨论：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 强调了 Debian 重建过程中的 idempotent（幂等性）和 bootstrapped（自举）特性，指出需要解决非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的问题才能实现完全的重建。

• [lrvick] 的回应中隐含了对 Guix 工具链的认可，特别是其在供应链安全方面的严格性，并通过推荐 stagex.tools 提供了一个实际的工具选择。

争议焦点：Debian main 是否已经因为非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的存在而无法自我重建，以及如何有效解决这些问题以确保其重建能力和安全性。

43534143.article_content:
I rebuilt (the top-50 popcon) Debian and Ubuntu packages, on amd and arm64, and
compared the results a couple of months ago
. Since then the
Reproduce.Debian.net
effort has been launched. Unlike my small experiment, that effort is a full-scale rebuild with more architectures. Their goal is to reproduce what is published in the
Debian
archive.
One differences between these two approaches are the build inputs: The Reproduce Debian effort use the same build inputs which were used to build the published packages. I’m using the latest version of published packages for the rebuild.
What does that difference imply? I believe
reproduce.debian.net
will be able to reproduce more of the packages in the archive. If you build a C program using one version of
GCC
you will get some binary output; and if you use a later GCC version you are likely to end up with a different binary output. This is a good thing: we want GCC to evolve and produce better output over time. However it means in order to reproduce the binaries we publish and use, we need to rebuild them using whatever build dependencies were used to prepare those binaries. The conclusion is that we need to use the old GCC to rebuild the program, and this appears to be the Reproduce.Debian.Net approach.
It would be a huge success if the Reproduce.Debian.net effort were to reach 100% reproducibility, and this seems to be within reach.
However I argue that we need go further than that. Being able to rebuild the packages reproducible using older binary packages only begs the question: can we rebuild those older packages? I fear attempting to do so ultimately leads to a need to rebuild 20+ year old packages, with a non-negligible amount of them being illegal to distribute or are unable to build anymore due to bit-rot. We won’t solve
the Trusting Trust concern
if our rebuild effort assumes some initial binary blob that we can no longer build from source code.
I’ve made an illustration of the effort I’m thinking of, to reach something that is stronger than reproducible rebuilds. I am calling this concept a Idempotent Rebuild, which is an old concept that I believe is the
same as John Gilmore has described
many years ago.
The illustration shows how the Debian main archive is used as input to rebuild another “stage #0” archive. This stage #0 archive can be compared with
diffoscope
to the main archive, and all differences are things that would be nice to resolve. The packages in the stage #0 archive is used to prepare a new container image with build tools, and the stage #0 archive is used as input to rebuild another version of itself, called the “stage #1” archive. The differences between stage #0 and stage #1 are also useful to analyse and resolve. This process can be repeated many times. I believe it would be a useful property if this process terminated at some point, where the stage #N archive was identical to the stage #N-1 archive. If this would happen, I label the output archive as an Idempotent Rebuild of the distribution.
How big is N today? The simplest assumption is that it is infinity. Any build timestamp embedded into binary packages will change on every iteration. This will cause the process to never terminate. Fixing embedded timestamps is something that the Reproduce.Debian.Net effort will also run into, and will have to resolve.
What other causes for differences could there be? It is easy to see that generally if some output is not deterministic, such as the sort order of assembler object code in binaries, then the output will be different. Trivial instances of this problem will be caught by the reproduce.debian.net effort as well.
Could there be higher order chains that lead to infinite N? It is easy to imagine the existence of these, but I don’t know how they would look like in practice.
An ideal would be if we could get down to N=1. Is that technically possible? Compare building GCC, it performs an initial stage 0 build using the system compiler to produce a stage 1 intermediate, which is used to build itself again to stage 2. Stage 1 and 2 is compared, and on success (identical binaries), the compilation succeeds. Here N=2. But this is performed using some unknown system compiler that is normally different from the GCC version being built. When rebuilding a binary distribution, you start with the same source versions. So it seems N=1 could be possible.
I’m unhappy to not be able to report any further technical progress now. The next step in this effort is to publish the stage #0 build artifacts in a repository, so they can be used to build stage #1. I already showed that stage #0 was around ~30% reproducible compared to the official binaries, but I didn’t save the artifacts in a reusable repository. Since the official binaries were not built using the latest versions, it is to be expected that the reproducibility number is low. But what happens at stage #1? data.title: Was Houdini a Spy? (2021)
data.author: carlos-menezes
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了著名魔术师哈里·胡迪尼是否曾从事间谍活动。胡迪尼以其逃脱魔术和 illusionist 技巧闻名，他的技术不仅影响了魔术界，也对情报和间谍活动产生了深远影响。文章提到，中央情报局（CIA）曾聘请魔术师约翰·穆赫兰，在冷战期间教授特工欺骗技术，这些技术部分源于胡迪尼的魔术。穆赫兰为CIA编写的手册在1973年被下令销毁，但后来被部分恢复并出版为《CIA官方诡计与欺骗手册》。胡迪尼的隐藏工具和逃脱技巧被认为启发了二战和冷战时期的间谍设备。一些历史学家，如《胡迪尼的秘密生活》的作者，认为胡迪尼可能参与了情报工作，包括向德国和英国警方提供信息以及协助美国特勤局打击伪钞。然而，胡迪尼是否真的是间谍仍无定论。

主要讨论点：关于魔术师与间谍活动的关联及历史事件的讨论

不同观点：

• [ggm] 对Jasper Maskelyne的评价存在争议，认为他的战争记录有争议，并将他的形象比作“胡萝卜有助于夜视”的宣传手段，暗示其作用被夸大。
• [neilv] 引用了MKULTRA项目的历史背景，批评文章没有提及CIA过去的负面事件，认为在当前时刻不应模糊过去的教训，强调需要警惕政府内部滥用权力。

补充讨论：
• [megadata] 提供了一个关于Houdini的播客链接，作为对Houdini相关讨论的补充资源。
• [pogue] 提供了《C.I.A.手册：诡计与欺骗》的链接，增加了对CIA使用魔术技巧进行间谍活动的实际案例的参考。
• [rmason] 分享了Houdini在万圣节去世的事实，并提到万圣节的魔术表演传统，为讨论增加了历史背景。
• [kmoser] 引用了James Randi的观点，质疑Houdini是否有可能作为间谍，并以Josephine Baker为例，暗示名人可能有隐藏的间谍身份。

争议焦点：
• 对Jasper Maskelyne的评价存在分歧，一方认为其作用被夸大，另一方则可能认可其技能在特定历史背景下的价值。
• 关于CIA文章是否应提及MKULTRA项目的负面历史，以及是否应在当前政治气候中强调这些教训，存在不同看法。

整体讨论展示了魔术师与间谍活动的交集，并触及了历史事件中的道德和政治争议。

Stories
Was Houdini a Spy?
October 29, 2021
Innovation and Tech
Contents
Point Down Icon
Introduction
Magic and Espionage at CIA
The Master of Deception, Harry Houdini
A Spy for America?
The worldâs most famous magician, Harry Houdini, was known as a celebrity conjurer, a practitioner of escape magic, and a master illusionist. Heâs had an enduring legacy on the magical arts since his untimely demise on Halloween Day, 1926. Thatâs why October 31
st
is known in magical circles as âNational Magic Dayâ or simply âHoudini Day.â
In honor of this legendary magician, weâre exploring the effect magic, and even Houdini, has had in the realms of intelligence and espionage.
Harry Houdini, courtesy of the Library of Congress
It may surprise people to learn that Houdiniâs magical techniques have influenced generations of clandestine officers. We even had a former CIA deputy director who was a magician himself!
But was Houdini more than just an influential figure?
Was he ever a practitioner in the art of espionage?
Was he a spy?
To answer these questions, we must first delve into the mystery of the missing magic manuals of Langley and the CIAâs first magician, John Mulholland.
Vintage poster for Harry Houdini show, courtesy of the Library of Congress.
Magic and Espionage at CIA
âMagic and espionage are really kindred arts,â or so wrote former CIA Deputy Director McLaughlin, an amateur magician himself, in the forward to the book, âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deceptionâ by H. Keith Melton and Robert Wallace.
This book, created from two long-lost training guides designed to teach Agency officers how to integrate elements of the magicianâs craft into clandestine operations, revealed that the CIAâs connection to the world of magic was decades old.
In the 1950s, as part of the MKULTRA project, the Agency hired magician John Mulholland to teach young officers techniques of deception suitable for the field, such as smuggling assets out of East Germany during the Cold War in vehicles that resembled the magic boxes used in stage illusions.
As part of his contract, Mulholland prepared two training manuals; âSome Operational Applications of the Art of Deceptionâ and âRecognition Signals.â
In 1973, when then-CIA Director Richard Helms ordered the destruction of all documents associated with the MKULTRA program, the manuals were thought to be gone forever.
Then, in 2007 while going through some unrelated documents, Robert Wallace, a former director of the CIAâs Office of Technical Services, discovered references to the manuals and tracked down poor-quality copies of each that had somehow escaped the shredder.
Believing that the manuals merited publication in full, Wallace conferred with his co-author, intelligence historian and collector Keith Melton, to produce âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deception,â which included illustrations of stage deception techniques, such as Harry Houdiniâs walk through a wall.
In fact, many of Houdiniâs magical escape techniques are discussed in the now declassified manuals, as they have influenced later generations of clandestine officers as well as spy gadgetry developed during the Cold War.
According to the Trickery and Deception book, concealment devises like magic coins and the hollow Mokana shoe used by Houdini for hiding escape tools became popular among spies throughout the Cold War era.
Even the Office of Strategic Services, the CIAâs WWII predecessor, was inspired by Houdini when they created tiny tools that mirrored those first used by the magician in his concealed escape kits.
Itâs no wonder then that many historians of magic and intelligence have found themselves pondering the question: Was Harry Houdiniâ¦
a spy?
Hungarian born magician and escapologist Harry Houdini (1874 – 1926) being fitted into an escape proof suit.   (Photo by MPI/Getty Images)
The Master of Deception, Harry Houdini
Since Houdiniâs death, there has been an on-going debate among historians as to whether or not Houdini was ever a âspy.â
The greatestÂ and most recent kerfuffle was theÂ publication in 2006 of âThe Secret Life of Houdini: The Making of Americaâs First Superheroâ by William Kalush and Larry Sloman, who conducted exhaustive research into the history of magic, eventually creating a fully text-searchable database of 700,000 pages of material, which contains thousands of references to Houdini.
Kalush and Sloman posit that the only reason Houdini would abruptly leave the United States in 1900, when he had finally achieved notorietyâand a paycheck equivalent to $45,000 a weekâwas because he was engaged in espionage. Houdini was rumored to be providing the German police with information about wanted criminals, as well as unspecified information to Scotland Yard Superintendent William Melville, monitoring anarchists in Russia, and helping the U.S. Secret Service with their anti-counterfeiting mission.

data.title: The Mainframe Vocabulary Problem, and Why It Matters
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术社区中的专业术语（jargon）和缩写对新手的可接近性以及其影响

不同观点：
• **don-code**：认为软件各领域都有自己的共享词汇，有助于提高沟通效率。一些社区（如DevOps、Python、Ruby、Rust）对新手很友好，使用易懂的语言。然而，安全和网络社区则充斥着缩略词，且部分从业者以知晓这些术语为荣，形成了不友好的氛围。
• **kotaKat**：认为虽然专业术语是平台力量的一部分，但需要有意识地去教。许多时候解释只停留在“是什么”，而没有深入“为什么”。并且，一些“守门人”式的态度阻碍了新手学习。
• **pjmlp**：认为技术领域充斥缩略词是普遍现象，并不局限于某个特定领域。
• **GianFabien**：指出年轻的技术人员更喜欢用AI、ML、GPT等流行缩略词，忽视了如COBOL、Java等“古老”技术。这反映了某种文化现象，可能让新手难以接触到传统但重要的技术知识。
• **classichasclass**：指出IBM词汇不仅仅限于大型主机，IBM的中端系统也使用类似的术语，如“IPL”。
• **Frummy**：提到随着AI的发展，现在学习这些专业术语和概念可能比过去容易得多。
• **rbanffy**：提供了一个IBM文档链接，帮助理解相关术语。
• **jgalt212**：幽默地指出文章未提到“WENUS”这个术语，暗示对某些内容的遗漏。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：技术社区中使用专业术语和缩略词的合理性。一部分人认为这些术语有助于高效沟通，另一部分人则认为它们形成了新手进入的障碍，尤其是在某些特定社区（如安全和网络）。
- **文化现象**：年轻技术人员更倾向于使用当前流行的技术术语，而忽视或不了解传统技术，这可能影响知识的传承和社区的包容性。
- **教学问题**：强调了不仅要解释“是什么”，还要解释“为什么”，以帮助新手更好地理解和融入技术社区。
- **具体例子**：如DevOps、Python等社区对新手友好，而安全和网络社区则存在不友好的现象。IBM系统中“IPL”等术语的使用范围也被讨论。

总体而言，评论主要围绕技术社区的专业术语和缩略词对新手的影响，以及如何更好地进行知识传承和社区建设。

• **kotaKat**：认为虽然专业术语是平台力量的一部分，但需要有意识地去教。许多时候解释只停留在“是什么”，而没有深入“为什么”。并且，一些“守门人”式的态度阻碍了新手学习。
• **pjmlp**：认为技术领域充斥缩略词是普遍现象，并不局限于某个特定领域。
• **GianFabien**：指出年轻的技术人员更喜欢用AI、ML、GPT等流行缩略词，忽视了如COBOL、Java等“古老”技术。这反映了某种文化现象，可能让新手难以接触到传统但重要的技术知识。
• **classichasclass**：指出IBM词汇不仅仅限于大型主机，IBM的中端系统也使用类似的术语，如“IPL”。
• **Frummy**：提到随着AI的发展，现在学习这些专业术语和概念可能比过去容易得多。
• **rbanffy**：提供了一个IBM文档链接，帮助理解相关术语。
• **jgalt212**：幽默地指出文章未提到“WENUS”这个术语，暗示对某些内容的遗漏。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：技术社区中使用专业术语和缩略词的合理性。一部分人认为这些术语有助于高效沟通，另一部分人则认为它们形成了新手进入的障碍，尤其是在某些特定社区（如安全和网络）。
- **文化现象**：年轻技术人员更倾向于使用当前流行的技术术语，而忽视或不了解传统技术，这可能影响知识的传承和社区的包容性。
- **教学问题**：强调了不仅要解释“是什么”，还要解释“为什么”，以帮助新手更好地理解和融入技术社区。
- **具体例子**：如DevOps、Python等社区对新手友好，而安全和网络社区则存在不友好的现象。IBM系统中“IPL”等术语的使用范围也被讨论。

总体而言，评论主要围绕技术社区的专业术语和缩略词对新手的影响，以及如何更好地进行知识传承和社区建设。

• **neilwilson**：认为在中国生产游戏的成本以人民币计算，而不是美元，且当前汇率需要从1:7调整到1:14，才能使中国继续成为可行的生产来源。他还提到中国主权财富基金需要更慷慨地提供人民币。

• **Gollapalli**：质疑在美国印刷和出版这些游戏的实际成本，认为主要材料不过是层压纸板和一些树脂件，质疑高成本的合理性。

data.title: Building Gearbox Dynamometer
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者Mateo Peña Doll自制了一个齿轮箱测功机（dynamometer），用于测试他设计和制造的船用变速箱。这些变速箱主要用于电动水翼船的较低单元齿轮箱。由于外包测试成本高昂（每小时100美元以上），作者决定自制一个AC测功机，以进行长达1000小时的耐久性测试。

该测功机包括8020铝框架、电机控制器调校、应变片校准等，并集成了自定义扭矩测量、水冷却、CAN总线以及基于Python的仪表板。测功机通过输入电机提供动力，再生电机输出动力，系统效率约为70%。它能连续处理30kW功率，峰值达50kW。

传感器测量包括扭矩、速度、温度、内部齿轮箱压力等数据，所有数据通过Arduino采集，并使用MongoDB进行存储和分析，通过Python仪表板实时监控。作者的自制方案有效降低了成本，并提供了丰富的数据支持变速箱测试。

43577927.article_content:
Search
Gearbox Dynamometer
ThriftyBuilder
7 days ago
7 min read
Updated:
2 days ago
Author: Mateo Peña Doll
I built this custom gearbox dynamometer (aka dyno) to test marine transmissions I design and build from the ground up. Typically, my transmissions serve as a lower-unit gearbox for hydrofoiling electric boats.
As a consulting mechanical engineer in the electric marine industry, I needed a way to run up to
1000 hours of durability testing
on the transmissions I develop. But with dyno labs charging $100+ per hour, outsourcing was not an option for me. The solution? Build my own
AC Dynamometer
. What started as a necessity quickly turned into a fully integrated, data-driven test rig, complete with custom torque measurement, water cooling, CAN bus integration, and a Python-based dashboard.
This project became a thesis-level deep dive into mechanical testing. From designing the 8020 aluminum frame, tuning motor controllers, to calibrating strain gauges, I picked up what felt like a degree in control systems and test engineering. Many things I learned the hard way. This post is all about the dyno itself:
how I built it, the challenges I ran into, and the technical details behind getting it to work.
Dyno Overview
Left to right: Input Motor (aka Drive) with a vertical shaft going into the gearbox. Out from the gearbox is a dynamic torque sensor, then a belt reduction (increasing speed). After the belt is the Output Motor (aka Dyno, or Regen).
In essence, this dyno measures the shaft power into the gearbox, and shaft power out.
Shaft power = torque * speed
. With the right parameters, I can simulate anything from light cruising loads to full-throttle acceleration, while monitoring how the gearbox is performing.
The dyno system works by inputting power to the Drive Motor, and then regenerating power output from the Dyno Motor. The system has a variety of losses, mechanical and electrical, so the regenerated power is a fraction of the input power (about 70% overall efficiency at optimal conditions). The approximately 30% losses end up coming from the 220VAC split-phase input to the power supplies (from the grid, costing money). I'll talk more about the power supplies below. The dyno can handle about
30kW continuous, and 50kW peak
at the Drive Motor.
Power Cables Schematic (DR is Drive, DY is Dyno/Regen)
I selected PMAC motors in the power range I needed, ultimately going with the Motenergy ME1616. For control, I chose Sevcon Gen4 Size 6 controllers, well-documented and widely used. Getting the ME1616 to work with the Sevcons required tuning using the Sevcon DVT tool. At this point I am versed in Sevcon DVT. Many thanks to
Motenergy
and the
Endless-Sphere
forums for supporting me with motor control information and config files.
Sensors
Measuring torque and speed was not trivial, and beyond that, several other parameters track system behavior. All data is captured using an Arduino-based DAQ system running my custom program.
Torque & Speed - Measured at both the gearbox input and output shafts
Efficiency - Output shaft power divided by input shaft power
Temperatures - housings, oil, water, and ambient
Internal Gearbox Pressure
Since the Sevcon controllers have their own slew of data, and require monitoring / calibration, I also monitor:
Motor and Controller Temperatures
Voltages and Currents
Motor Velocities and Torques (reported)
Many other minutia
Arduino Due based DAQ system
For sensors, I used low-cost, Arduino-compatible modules. The Arduino Due captures sensor data, transmits it via CAN bus, and also acts as an error detector and fault trigger, stopping the system if needed. Each sensor had it's own communication protocols, noise sensitivities, and posed unique challenges for me to setup. I go into more details about learnings and future improvements at the end of this post.
Torque Sensor: Daysensor DYN-200 (500 Nm, 4-20mA output)
Strain Gauge Amplifier: SparkFun SEN-13879 (HX711 based) - love these!
Pressure Sensor: Honeywell HSCSANN015PA2A3 (I2C)
Current Sensor: Adafruit INA228 (I2C) - Unfortunately I never actually got this one to work
Thermocouple Amplifier: Adafruit 1778 (AD8495, K-Type)
CAN Transceiver: Copperhill SN65HVD230
Dashboard and Database
Managing all 50+ data points required setting up an automated data collection system using MongoDB, which stores everything for post-analysis. To manage the database and monitor the data real-time, I built a custom Python dashboard using Tkinter, with CAN bus integration using an IXXAT to USB converter. Special thanks to ChatGPT for doing most of the leg work on the coding :)
Controls and Data Diagram
Custom Python Dashboard

The way I provided 10kW of power to the dyno was thrifty, if I may say so myself. As mentioned, the system runs at about 70% efficiency under optimal conditions, and the Drive Motor power requirement (input power to the gearbox) was set at 30kW continuous. That meant I needed at least
